title: SAST: Ruby scans analyse no files (built-in `tmp` exclusion matches the clone path /tmp/repo_*)
body:
**Severity:** high. A customer's Ruby SAST scan silently analyses zero files and reports a clean result.

**Root cause.** `file_path_matches_pattern` (worker `codebase_context.py`) matches the built-in and customer exclusion patterns against the **absolute** path. The worker clones or unzips into `/tmp/repo_*`, so Ruby's built-in exclusion `tmp` matches every file. Unanchored patterns over-match in other ways too: the documented example `.min.js` also excludes `src/routes/admin.js` (the `.` is a regex wildcard).

**Reproduction (inside `dss-staging-scan-worker-1`, worker venv):** `CodebaseContext.load_documents_of_extension` on a throw-away `/tmp/repo_x` with `app/models/user.rb` and `src/routes/admin.js` returns `RUBY defaults: included [] excluded ['<clone>/app/models/user.rb']`. In the same run, the pattern `.min.js` excluded `admin.js`.

**Expected.** Patterns match the path *relative to the repository root*, with glob semantics (or escaped regex), so `tmp` only excludes a top-level or nested `tmp/` directory inside the repo, and `.min.js` only matches minified files.

**Fix.** Make the matcher work on the repo-relative path and use explicit glob semantics. Add unit tests for every language's built-in exclusions with the clone under `/tmp/`, plus the `.min.js` case. Related: #37 (include/exclude patterns), which this extends.

Found by the content-accuracy review of PR #38 (review 5858670025). Evidence scripts: session scratchpad `round6/rv-content38-probe/`.
